We differentiate the given function with respect to $x,$ treating all other variables as constants. 

First, we use the chain rule: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂f}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}((x+1)^{{y}^{2}}) \\  & ={y}^{2}(x+1)^{{y}^{2}-1}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the sum rule for differentiation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{2}(x+1)^{{y}^{2}-1}\cdot \frac{∂}{∂x}(x+1) & ={y}^{2}(x+1)^{{y}^{2}-1}\cdot (\frac{∂}{∂x}(x)+\frac{∂}{∂x}(1)) \\  & ={y}^{2}(x+1)^{{y}^{2}-1}\cdot (1+0) \\  & ={y}^{2}(x+1)^{{y}^{2}-1}\end{aligned}
$$
